inputs.name: Camestros: average is not fastest
inputs.quote: If the figure is an average then it includes some mutations that fixed quicker and so is not the fastest fixed mutation rate.

inputs.name: Camestros concession: an average
inputs.quote: He is correct that when he calculated the number it was an average.

inputs.name: Duffy relaying Day: 180 at the fastest rate
inputs.quote: 180 total fixed mutations is all there's time for using the fastest rate of mutational fixation ever observed in any organism

inputs.name: 2nd-edition abstract: 1,400 the fastest
inputs.quote: 1,400 generations per fixation (the fastest empirical rate ever measured in any organism)

inputs.name: no mammalian fixation faster than 1,600
inputs.quote: No one has ever observed any human or even mammalian fixation faster than 1,600 generations.

inputs.name: mutator rates in the 3.0 tables
inputs.cite: claim file A2d formal statement (Z23003785 s5.1, s7.2)

day.reading: 'fastest' means the throughput rate of the applicable non-mutator class; an average is the right quantity to multiply by time (Camestros concedes the average, CA-10)
day.caveat: among Day's own non-mutator figures the clone-pair 893 is faster than 1,322 (1.48x) and 1,400 (1.57x)

critic.reading: a mean cannot be the fastest rate; the LTEE's point-mutator populations fix at 43-183 gen/fix

positions.window: 1,600 generations at 25 y is 40,000 y, longer than any direct observation of human allele-frequency change, so 'no faster fixation observed' cannot separate a slow rate from a short window
